text:
alex-support: Customer reported embeddings endpoint returning 1024 dims but their index expects 1536. They get a mismatch error and failing upsert to vector DB.

sam-eng: can you paste the raw request body they sent and the exact error text?

alex-support: Error from client library: \"DimensionMismatch: expected 1536, got 1024\". Customer attached this payload snippet: 
```json
{
  \"input\": [[\"Search term here\"]]
}
```

lina-sre: whoa nested arrays. Looks like double-wrapping to me. Our embeddings models return 1536 for embed-large; 1024 sounds like they fed something else (maybe sent token counts instead?) or the client unrolled something.

sam-eng: also possible their local batching logic collapsed strings into a single concatenated string per batch and they used a smaller model by accident. ask if they hard-coded model param.

alex-support: customer says they call our hosted endpoint via fetch in a worker. snippet they shared: 
```js
const body = JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify(batch) });
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body, headers });
```
They said they were \"just wrapping the batch\" because the SDK was failing earlier.

lina-sre: yeah that's the bug — double JSON.stringify. That turns their array into a single string, which our server treats as one long string, then the client lib (or DB upsert) later tries to parse and ends up feeding a different embedding or a compressed vector.

sam-eng: repro steps I used locally: 1) send correct batch: `{\"input\":[\"a\",\"b\"]}` -> returns two embeddings 1536 each. 2) send double-wrapped: `{\"input\":\"[\\\"a\\\",\\\"b\\\"]\"}` -> server returns one embedding (1536) but the client app incorrectly splits it and mis-attributes length leading to 1024 read by DB adapter. Strange but customer stack did a reduce that trimmed vector to 1024.

alex-support: customer also saw a billing spike because retries kicked in when DB upsert failed. They saw multiple 200s from embedding but 400s from DB.

lina-sre: next steps for support reply: 1) ask them to switch to `body: JSON.stringify({input: batch})` (no extra stringify). 2) share a minimal curl repro. 3) suggest turning on request logging to confirm shape. 4) patch DB upsert to validate dims and return a clearer error.

sam-eng: paste curl we can give them:
```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings\" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"input\":[\"alpha\",\"beta\"], \"model\":\"embed-large\" }'
```

alex-support: replied to customer with that curl + explanation and asked for full request/response dump. Also warned about retry loops and suggested exponential backoff. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident-note: lowered severity — root cause client-side double-encode; no server regressions. Logged for docs update: add example for common JS pitfall.

lina-sre: I'll open a tiny docs PR to add a \"JS fetch double-stringify\" example and a note to validate dims before DB upsert.

sam-eng: agree. also add a quick troubleshooting checklist to support playbook: check model param, verify input shape (list vs string), avoid double stringify, inspect vector length before DB write.

alex-support: customer confirmed fix after removing extra stringify; dims now 1536 and DB ingest succeeded. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
